dimensions.assessment: Affects federal agencies such as the U.S. Secret Service, FinCEN, GAO, and financial institutions involved in information-sharing partnerships.
dimensions.evidence: authorizes the Secret Service to investigate money laundering and structured transactions

dimensions.assessment: Changes investigative jurisdictions and extends reporting timelines rather than creating sweeping personal or commercial disruption.
dimensions.evidence: Section 310(d)(3)(A) of title 31, United States Code, is amended, in the matter preceding clause (i), by striking '5 years' and inserting '10 years'.

dimensions.assessment: No specific federal spending or revenue amounts are stated in the source text.
Amends existing federal statutes related to Secret Service powers, FinCEN reporting, and mandates a new GAO study.
dimensions.evidence: Section 3056(b) of title 18, United States Code, is amended

dimensions.assessment: Extends certain reporting mandates to 10 years and adds permanent statutory authority for Secret Service investigations.

missing_information: Specific fiscal estimates or appropriations authorized by the bill.
importance_detail.rationale: The bill expands the investigative authorities of the U.S. Secret Service regarding digital assets and money laundering, extends reporting requirements for FinCEN and international financial institutions, and requires a GAO report, creating limited administrative and oversight changes.
